## Invoice intake and scheduling

POST /v1/invoices returns HTTP 202 with data.props and initial status queued.
options.type accepts IMMEDIATE (default) or SCHEDULE. SCHEDULE uses a future
competenceDate (YYYY-MM-DD) and releases emission at 00:00 America/Sao_Paulo.
data.props.scheduledFor is the release timestamp (ISO string), or null for
IMMEDIATE; scheduled invoices remain queued until that instant. Dates beyond
the configured horizon (15 days by default) return HTTP 422 with fiscal issue
code schedule_horizon_exceeded. Intake atomically persists invoice, event and
outbox message. Once a queue publication is acknowledged, a Redis reset can
lose the job while the invoice stays queued; document recovery does not recover
queued invoices.

## Fiscal engine (IBS/CBS and ISS)

Every queued invoice runs a fail-fast fiscal pipeline (company fiscal profile,
service classification, tax applicability, ISS/withholding, RTC/IBS-CBS,
validator) driven by the transactional outbox (type invoice.calculate-taxes).
The company's tax regime now comes from the historical company_fiscal_profiles
table, not nfse_companies. customer is optional (omitted => consumidor, no
tomador in the DPS); discount and service.fiscal are accepted at intake. IBS/CBS
is delegated to the official RTC calculator whose real adapter is not yet built
(Spec 3), so with FISCAL_IBSCBS_UNAVAILABLE_MODE=block (default) invoices whose
IBS/CBS is mandatory are rejected with lastErrorCode TAX_CALCULATION_UNAVAILABLE
instead of emitting incomplete notes. The computed result is persisted as an
immutable invoice_fiscal_snapshots row. This engine is always on (no feature
flag).
